1.1: The Lord called Moses from the Tabernacle and told him,
1.2: "Aight, tell the people of Israel this—when y'all bring an animal as an offering to Me, it gotta come from your herd of cattle, or your flock of sheep and goats.
1.3: If you bringing a bull for a burnt offering, it gotta be a male with no defects. Bring it to the entrance of the Tabernacle, so the Lord can accept you.
1.4: Put your hand on the animal's head, and the Lord will take it as a stand-in for you—it's gonna purify you and make you right with Him.
1.5: Then y'all gotta slaughter the young bull in the Lord's presence, and Aaron's sons—the priests—will take the blood and splash it on all sides of the altar at the Tabernacle entrance.
1.6: After that, skin the animal and cut it up.
1.7: The sons of Aaron will set up a fire on the altar,
1.8: and they'll lay the pieces—including the head and the fat—on the burning wood.
1.9: But before that, the internal organs and the legs gotta be washed with water. Then the priest will burn the whole thing on the altar as a burnt offering. It's a special gift, something that smells real good to the Lord.
1.10: If you bringing a sheep or a goat for a burnt offering, it gotta be a male with no defects.
1.11: Slaughter it on the north side of the altar, right in front of the Lord, and Aaron's sons will splash its blood on all sides of the altar.
1.12: Then cut it into pieces, and the priests will arrange the parts—including the head and fat—on the burning wood.
1.13: The insides and legs gotta be washed first, and then the priest will burn the whole thing as a burnt offering. It's a special gift, and it's a pleasing smell to the Lord.
1.14: If you bringing a bird as a burnt offering, make sure it's either a turtledove or a young pigeon.
1.15: The priest will take it to the altar, wring its head off, and burn it there. But first, he gotta drain the blood on the side of the altar.
1.16: Then he'll take out the bird's crop and feathers and toss them in the ashes on the east side of the altar.
1.17: Finally, he'll grab the bird by its wings and tear it open—but not all the way apart—and then burn it on the altar's wood fire. Just like the other offerings, it's a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

2.1: If you bring a grain offering to the Lord, it gotta be the finest flour. Pour olive oil on it and sprinkle some frankincense on top.
2.2: Then take it to Aaron's sons, the priests. One of them will grab a handful of that flour, mix it with the oil and all the frankincense, and burn it on the altar. This offering is a special gift, and the smell pleases the Lord.
2.3: The rest of the grain offering goes to Aaron and his sons. This part of the offering is real holy—one of the special gifts set apart for the Lord.
2.4: If you baking your grain offering in an oven, it gotta be made from the finest flour, no yeast allowed. You can bring it as thin cakes mixed with olive oil or wafers brushed with oil.
2.5: If you cooking your grain offering on a griddle, it still gotta be made with the finest flour and olive oil, but no yeast.
2.6: Break it into pieces and pour some olive oil on it. That's your grain offering.
2.7: If your grain offering is made in a pan, same rule—use the finest flour and olive oil.
2.8: No matter how you make your grain offering, bring it to the priest, and he'll take it to the altar.
2.9: The priest will grab a handful from it and burn that portion on the altar as a special gift. The smell gonna be real pleasing to the Lord.
2.10: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons as their food. It's a most holy part of the special gifts offered to the Lord.
2.11: Don't use no yeast when making any grain offering to the Lord. And don't be adding honey either, cause neither of them can be burned as an offering to the Lord.
2.12: If you bringing a first-fruits offering from your harvest, you can use yeast and honey, but you can't put that on the altar as a burnt offering that's supposed to smell good to the Lord.
2.13: Make sure you season all your grain offerings with salt, cause that salt is a reminder of God's eternal covenant. Don't ever forget to add salt to your offerings.
2.14: If you bringing a grain offering from the first part of your harvest, bring fresh grain that's been roasted and coarsely crushed.
2.15: Pour some olive oil on it and sprinkle some frankincense over it.
2.16: The priest will take a handful of that grain mixed with oil, along with all the frankincense, and burn it on the altar as a special gift to the Lord.

3.1: If you bringing an animal from the herd as a peace offering to the Lord, it can be a male or a female, but it gotta be without any defects.
3.2: Put your hand on the animal's head and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tabernacle. Then Aaron's sons, the priests, gonna take the blood and splash it on all sides of the altar.
3.3: The priest gotta take some of this peace offering as a special gift to the Lord. That includes all the fat around the internal organs,
3.4: The two kidneys, the fat around them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver—these gotta be removed with the kidneys.
3.5: Aaron's sons will burn these parts on top of the burnt offering, over the wood burning on the altar. This offering is a special gift, and the Lord gonna love the smell.
3.6: If you bringing an animal from the flock as a peace offering to the Lord, it can be a male or a female, but it gotta be without defects.
3.7: If you offering a sheep, bring it before the Lord,
3.8: Put your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tabernacle. Aaron's sons will then splash its blood on all sides of the altar.
3.9: The priest gotta take the fat of this peace offering as a special gift to the Lord. That includes the fat of the broad tail cut off near the backbone, all the fat around the internal organs,
3.10: The two kidneys, the fat around them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver—these must be removed with the kidneys.
3.11: The priest will burn them on the altar as a special gift of food to the Lord.
3.12: If you bringing a goat as a peace offering, bring it before the Lord,
3.13: Put your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tabernacle. Aaron's sons will then splash its blood on all sides of the altar.
3.14: The priest gotta take some of this offering as a special gift to the Lord. That includes all the fat around the internal organs,
3.15: The two kidneys, the fat around them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver—these gotta be removed with the kidneys.
3.16: The priest will burn them on the altar as a special gift of food, a smell the Lord gonna love. All the fat belongs to the Lord.
3.17: Y'all must never eat no fat or blood. This rule stays forever, for every generation, no matter where y'all live.

4.2: Go tell the people of Israel how to handle things when somebody sins on accident, breaking one of the Lord's commands without knowing.
4.3: If the high priest messes up and brings guilt on the whole community, he gotta bring a young bull with no defects as a sin offering for what he did.
4.4: He gotta bring that bull to the entrance of the Tabernacle, put his hand on its head, and kill it right there before the Lord.
4.5: Then the high priest will take some of the bull's blood inside the Tabernacle,
4.6: Dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times in front of the inner curtain in the sanctuary.
4.7: After that, he'll put some of the blood on the horns of the incense altar inside the Tabernacle, in the Lord's presence. The rest of the blood? He gonna pour that out at the base of the burnt offering altar at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
4.8: Then he gotta take all the fat from the bull as part of the sin offering—
4.9: That means the fat around the internal organs, the two kidneys, the fat around the loins, and the long lobe of the liver.
4.10: He gotta remove them just like he would for a peace offering and burn them on the burnt offering altar.
4.11: But the rest of the bull—the hide, the meat, the head, legs, internal organs, and even the dung—
4.12: He gotta take all of that outside the camp to the special clean place where the ashes get dumped. He will burn it there on a wood fire at the ash heap.
4.13: If the whole Israelite community messes up and breaks one of the Lord's commands without knowing, they still guilty.
4.14: When they realize what they did, they gotta bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it in front of the Tabernacle.
4.15: The community elders will put their hands on the bull's head and kill it before the Lord.
4.16: Then the high priest will take some of the bull's blood inside the Tabernacle,
4.17: Dip his finger in it, and sprinkle it seven times in front of the inner curtain.
4.18: He will then put some of the blood on the horns of the incense altar inside the Tabernacle, and pour the rest of the blood out at the base of the burnt offering altar at the entrance.
4.19: Then he gotta take all the fat off and burn it on the altar,
4.20: Just like he did for the high priest's sin offering. That's how the priest makes things right for the people, and they will be forgiven.
4.21: Then he gotta take the rest of the bull outside the camp and burn it, just like the high priest's sin offering. This is for the whole congregation's sin.
4.22: If one of Israel's leaders messes up and breaks a command without realizing, he still guilty.
4.23: When he finds out what he did, he gotta bring a male goat with no defects as his sin offering.
4.24: He'll put his hand on the goat's head and kill it at the same place as the burnt offerings, before the Lord.
4.25: Then the priest will dip his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar. The rest of the blood? He will pour it out at the base of the altar.
4.26: Then he will burn all the fat on the altar just like he would for a peace offering. That's how the priest makes things right for the leader, and he will be forgiven.
4.27: If any regular person sins by breaking one of the Lord's commands without knowing, they still guilty.
4.28: When they find out what they did, they gotta bring a female goat with no defects as a sin offering.
4.29: They'll put their hand on the goat's head and kill it where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.
4.30: Then the priest will dip his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar. The rest of the blood? He will pour it out at the base of the altar.
4.31: Then he will take all the fat off, just like with a peace offering, and burn it on the altar. The smell gonna be pleasing to the Lord. That's how the priest makes things right for the person, and they will be forgiven.
4.32: If they bring a sheep as their sin offering, it gotta be a female with no defects.
4.33: They'll put their hand on its head and kill it at the place where burnt offerings get slaughtered.
4.34: Then the priest will dip his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar. The rest of the blood? He will pour it out at the base of the altar.
4.35: Then he gotta remove all the fat, just like he would with a peace offering, and burn it on top of the special gifts presented to the Lord. That's how the priest makes things right for them, and they will be forgiven.

5.1: If you get called to testify about something you seen or know about, and you refuse to speak up, that's a sin. You gonna be held accountable for that.
5.2: If you accidentally touch something that's unclean—like a dead animal that ain't supposed to be eaten—once you realize what you did, you gotta admit you made yourself unclean.
5.3: Same thing if you touch something that makes a person unclean. When you realize it, you gotta acknowledge your guilt.
5.4: If you make a reckless vow—whether it's to do something good or bad—and later realize it was foolish, you gotta admit your guilt.
5.5: Whenever you become aware of your sin in any of these ways, you gotta confess what you did.
5.6: Then you gotta bring a female sheep or goat from your flock as a sin offering. The priest will use it to purify you and make things right with the Lord.
5.7: If you can't afford a sheep, you can bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons instead—one for a sin offering, the other for a burnt offering.
5.8: Take them to the priest. He will offer the first bird for the sin offering by wringing its neck, but he won't pull the head off completely.
5.9: He'll sprinkle some of the blood against the sides of the altar and drain the rest at the base. That's the sin offering.
5.10: Then he will prepare the second bird as a burnt offering, following the usual rules. This way, the priest will purify you, making things right with the Lord, and you will be forgiven.
5.11: If you can't afford two birds, you can bring about two quarts of fine flour as your sin offering. But don't mix it with oil or put frankincense on it, cause it's a sin offering.
5.12: Take the flour to the priest. He will take a handful and burn it on the altar on top of the special gifts for the Lord. This is the sin offering.
5.13: Through this process, the priest will purify you from any of these sins, making things right with the Lord, and you will be forgiven. The rest of the flour belongs to the priest, just like the grain offering.
5.15: If you accidentally mess up and disrespect something sacred that belongs to the Lord, you gotta bring a guilt offering. That means bringing a ram with no defects—or buying one of equal value with silver, using the sanctuary shekel for measurement.
5.16: You also gotta pay back what you messed up, plus an extra 20 percent. When you give it to the priest, he will purify you by sacrificing the ram as a guilt offering, making things right with the Lord. Then you'll be forgiven.
5.17: If you break one of the Lord's commands, even if you didn't know you messed up, you're still guilty and gotta face the consequences.
5.18: For a guilt offering, you gotta bring a ram with no defects, or buy one of equal value. The priest will use it to purify you from your unintentional sin, making things right with the Lord, and you'll be forgiven.
5.19: This is a guilt offering, cause you been guilty of an offense against the Lord.

6.2: If somebody sins against their neighbor, they also being unfaithful to the Lord. That means if they cheat somebody in a deal, steal, or commit fraud,
6.3: Or if they find lost property and lie about it, or swear to tell the truth but still lie, or do anything shady like that—
6.4: If they guilty of any of these things, they gotta pay back what they stole, took by fraud, kept from somebody, or lied about.
6.5: They gotta return the full amount plus an extra 20 percent to the person they wronged. And on that same day, they gotta bring a guilt offering.
6.6: For their guilt offering, they gotta bring a ram with no defects to the priest, or buy one of equal value.
6.7: Then the priest will purify them before the Lord, making things right, and they'll be forgiven for whatever sin they committed.
6.9: Tell Aaron and his sons these instructions about burnt offerings. The burnt offering gotta stay on the altar all night until morning, and the fire must keep burning the whole time.
6.10: In the morning, the priest on duty will put on his linen clothes and undergarments, then clean out the ashes from the burnt offering and put them beside the altar.
6.11: Then he'll change back into his regular clothes and take the ashes outside the camp to a place that's clean.
6.12: Meanwhile, the fire on the altar must never go out. Every morning, the priest will add fresh wood, arrange the burnt offering, and burn the fat from the peace offerings.
6.13: That fire gotta stay burning on the altar—it must never go out.
6.14: These the instructions for the grain offering. Aaron's sons gotta present it before the Lord, in front of the altar.
6.15: The priest on duty will grab a handful of the best flour, mix it with olive oil, and add all the frankincense. Then he'll burn this portion on the altar, and the smell will please the Lord.
6.16: Aaron and his sons can eat the rest of the flour, but it gotta be baked without yeast and eaten in a holy place inside the Tabernacle courtyard.
6.17: It must never be made with yeast, cause this is their portion of the Lord's special gifts, just like the sin offering and the guilt offering—it's most holy.
6.18: Any male descendant of Aaron can eat from these sacred offerings. This is their permanent right, passed down through generations. Anybody who touches these offerings will become holy.
6.20: On the day Aaron and his sons get anointed, they gotta bring a grain offering of two quarts of fine flour—half in the morning, half in the evening.
6.21: It gotta be mixed with olive oil and cooked on a griddle. Then it must be sliced up and presented as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
6.22: Every high priest after Aaron must prepare this same offering. It belongs to the Lord and must be completely burned up.
6.23: Every grain offering from a priest must be burned entirely—none of it can be eaten.
6.25: Tell Aaron and his sons: The sin offering is most holy, and it must be slaughtered in the Lord's presence at the same place where burnt offerings are killed.
6.26: The priest who offers the sacrifice must eat his portion in a sacred place inside the Tabernacle courtyard.
6.27: Anything or anyone that touches this sacrificial meat will become holy. If any of its blood splashes on somebody's clothes, they gotta wash that garment in a sacred place.
6.28: If the meat is boiled in a clay pot, that pot must be broken afterward. If it's cooked in a bronze pot, it gotta be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
6.29: Any male from a priest's family can eat this offering, cause it's most holy.
6.30: But if the blood from the sin offering is brought inside the Tabernacle for purification, then that offering can't be eaten—it gotta be completely burned with fire.

7.1: These the rules for the guilt offering. It's most holy.
7.2: The animal used for the guilt offering gotta be slaughtered in the same place as the burnt offerings, and its blood gotta be splattered on all sides of the altar.
7.3: The priest will take all the fat and burn it on the altar—this includes the fat from the broad tail and the fat around the internal organs.
7.4: The two kidneys, the fat near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver all gotta be removed with the kidneys.
7.5: The priests will burn these parts on the altar as a special gift to the Lord. This is the guilt offering.
7.6: Any male from a priest's family can eat the meat, but it gotta be eaten in a sacred place, cause it's most holy.
7.7: The same rules apply for both the guilt offering and the sin offering—both belong to the priest who offers them to purify someone before the Lord.
7.8: If it's a burnt offering, the priest who sacrifices it gets to keep the hide of the animal.
7.9: Any grain offering that's baked in an oven, cooked in a pan, or on a griddle belongs to the priest who presented it.
7.10: All other grain offerings, whether dry or mixed with olive oil, gotta be shared equally among Aaron's descendants—the priests.
7.11: These the rules for the different kinds of peace offerings people can bring to the Lord.
7.12: If it's a thanksgiving offering, it gotta come with bread made without yeast—thin cakes mixed with olive oil, wafers spread with oil, and cakes made with choice flour and olive oil.
7.13: This peace offering also gotta come with loaves of bread made with yeast.
7.14: One of each type of bread must be presented as a special gift to the Lord, and it will belong to the priest who splatters the blood of the peace offering on the altar.
7.15: The meat from this thanksgiving peace offering must be eaten on the same day. None of it can be saved for the next morning.
7.16: If the offering is for a vow or just a voluntary offering, the meat must be eaten the same day, but leftovers can be eaten the next day.
7.17: But any meat left until the third day gotta be completely burned up.
7.18: If anybody eats from the peace offering on the third day, it won't be accepted, and they won't get credit for the offering. By that time, the meat is contaminated, and if they eat it, they'll be punished for their sin.
7.19: If the meat touches anything unclean, it can't be eaten—it must be burned up. But if it's still clean, only people who are ceremonially clean can eat it.
7.20: If anybody who is unclean eats the peace offering meat, they gonna be cut off from the community.
7.21: If somebody touches anything unclean—whether it's a dead body, an unclean animal, or something nasty—and then eats from the peace offering, they gonna be cut off from the community.
7.23: Tell the Israelites never to eat the fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.
7.24: If an animal dies on its own or gets torn up by wild animals, its fat can be used for other purposes, but it can't be eaten.
7.25: Anybody who eats fat from an animal that was offered to the Lord as a gift will be cut off from the community.
7.26: No matter where y'all live, never eat the blood of any bird or animal.
7.27: Anybody who eats blood will be cut off from the community.
7.29: Tell the Israelites: When y'all bring a peace offering to the Lord, part of it gotta be set aside as a special gift.
7.30: You gotta bring the fat of the animal, along with the breast, and lift it up as a special offering to the Lord.
7.31: The priest will burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
7.32: The right thigh of the peace offering must be given to the priest as a special gift.
7.33: The right thigh always belongs to the priest who offers the blood and fat of the peace offering.
7.34: The Lord said: I have set aside the breast of the special offering and the right thigh of the sacred offering for the priests. This is their permanent portion from the peace offerings brought by the Israelites.
7.35: This is their rightful share—the special gifts that belong to Aaron and his descendants from the time they were chosen to serve as priests.
7.36: On the day they were anointed, the Lord commanded that these portions belong to the priests forever—from generation to generation.
7.37: These are the official instructions for the burnt offering, grain offering, sin offering, guilt offering, ordination offering, and peace offering.
7.38: The Lord gave all these instructions to Moses on Mount Sinai when He commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings in the wilderness.

8.2: Bring Aaron and his sons, their special robes, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of bread made without yeast.
8.3: Then call the whole community of Israel together at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
8.4: So Moses did what the Lord said, and the whole community gathered at the Tabernacle entrance.
8.5: Then Moses told them, 'This is what the Lord commanded us to do!'
8.6: Moses then brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
8.7: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around his waist, dressed him in the robe, put the ephod on him, and fastened it with its decorative sash.
8.8: Then Moses put the chestpiece on Aaron and placed the Urim and Thummim inside it.
8.9: He set the turban on Aaron's head and attached the gold medallion—the badge of holiness—to the front of the turban, just like the Lord commanded.
8.10: Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the Tabernacle and everything in it, making them holy.
8.11: He sprinkled the oil on the altar seven times, anointing it, all its tools, the washbasin, and its stand to make them holy.
8.12: Then he poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head, anointing him to set him apart for his work.
8.13: Next, Moses brought Aaron's sons forward. He dressed them in their tunics, tied their sashes around them, and put special head coverings on them, just as the Lord commanded.
8.14: Then Moses brought out the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
8.15: Moses killed the bull and took some of the blood, putting it on the four horns of the altar with his finger to purify it. Then he poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar to make it holy.
8.16: Moses then took all the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and burned them on the altar.
8.17: But the rest of the bull—including its hide, meat, and dung—was burned outside the camp, just like the Lord commanded.
8.18: Then Moses brought out the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
8.19: Moses slaughtered the ram and splattered its blood on all sides of the altar.
8.20: Then he cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat on the altar.
8.21: After washing the internal organs and legs with water, Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing smell, a special gift to the Lord, just as He commanded.
8.22: Then Moses brought out the second ram—the ordination ram—and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
8.23: Moses slaughtered it, then took some of its blood and put it on Aaron's right ear, right thumb, and right big toe.
8.24: Then Moses did the same for Aaron's sons, putting the blood on their right ears, right thumbs, and right big toes. Then he splattered the rest of the blood on all sides of the altar.
8.25: Then Moses took the fat from the broad tail, the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
8.26: On top of that, he placed a thin cake of bread made without yeast, a cake of bread mixed with olive oil, and a wafer spread with oil—all taken from the special basket in the Lord's presence.
8.27: He put all these in Aaron and his sons' hands and lifted them up as a special offering to the Lord.
8.28: Then Moses took all the offerings back and burned them on the altar, on top of the burnt offering. This was the ordination offering, a pleasing smell and a special gift to the Lord.
8.29: Then Moses took the breast of the ram and lifted it up as a special offering. That was his portion of the ordination offering, just like the Lord commanded.
8.30: Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his sons, along with their robes. This made them and their garments holy.
8.31: Then Moses told Aaron and his sons, 'Boil the rest of the meat at the Tabernacle entrance and eat it there, along with the bread from the ordination basket, just like the Lord commanded.'
8.32: If there's any leftover meat or bread, it must be completely burned up.
8.33: You can't leave the Tabernacle entrance for seven days—this is how long the ordination ceremony lasts.
8.34: Everything we did today was commanded by the Lord to purify you and make you right with Him.
8.35: Now, y'all gotta stay at the entrance of the Tabernacle day and night for seven days and do everything the Lord requires. If y'all don't follow through, you will die—that's the Lord's command.
8.36: So Aaron and his sons did everything the Lord commanded through Moses.

9.1: After the ordination ceremony, on the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel together.
9.2: Moses told Aaron, 'Go get a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. Both gotta be flawless. Present them to the Lord.'
9.3: Then tell the Israelites, 'Bring a male goat for a sin offering. Also, bring a calf and a lamb, both a year old and without defects, for a burnt offering.'
9.4: Bring a bull and a ram for a peace offering, along with some flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering. Present all this to the Lord, cause He gon' show up today.'
9.5: So the people brought everything to the entrance of the Tabernacle, just like Moses commanded. Then the whole community came forward and stood before the Lord.
9.6: Moses told them, 'This is what the Lord said to do, so His glory can show up among y'all.'
9.7: Then Moses told Aaron, 'Go up to the altar and sacrifice your sin offering and burnt offering to purify yourself and the people. Then offer the people's sacrifices so they can be made right with the Lord, just like He commanded.'
9.8: So Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the calf for his own sin offering.
9.9: His sons brought him the blood, and he dipped his finger in it and put it on the horns of the altar. Then he poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
9.10: Aaron burned the fat, kidneys, and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, just like the Lord told Moses.
9.11: But the rest of the bull—its meat and hide—he burned outside the camp.
9.12: Then Aaron killed the animal for the burnt offering. His sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it on all sides of the altar.
9.13: Then they handed him each piece of the burnt offering, including the head, and Aaron burned them on the altar.
9.14: He washed the internal organs and the legs, then burned them on the altar along with the rest of the burnt offering.
9.15: Next, Aaron presented the people's offerings. He killed the goat for their sin offering, just like he did for his own.
9.16: Then he presented the burnt offering and sacrificed it just like the Lord commanded.
9.17: He also presented the grain offering, burning a handful of the flour mixture on the altar, along with the usual morning burnt offering.
9.18: Then Aaron killed the bull and ram for the people's peace offering. His sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it on all sides of the altar.
9.19: Then he took the fat of the bull and ram—the broad tail, the fat around the internal organs, the kidneys, and the long lobes of the livers.
9.20: He placed the fat on top of the breasts of the animals and burned them on the altar.
9.21: Aaron then lifted up the breasts and right thighs as a special offering to the Lord, just like Moses commanded.
9.22: After that, Aaron raised his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then, after offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering, he stepped down from the altar.
9.23: Moses and Aaron then went inside the Tabernacle. When they came back out, they blessed the people again, and the glory of the Lord appeared to the whole community.
9.24: Suddenly, fire blazed out from the Lord's presence and burned up the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. When the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell face down on the ground.

10.1: Aaron's sons, Nadab and Abihu, grabbed their incense burners, put hot coals in them, and sprinkled incense over the top. But they disobeyed the Lord by burning the wrong kind of fire—something He ain't never told them to do.
10.2: So fire shot out from the Lord's presence and burned them up right there, and they died before the Lord.
10.3: Then Moses told Aaron, 'This what the Lord meant when He said: I will show My holiness through those close to Me. I will let My glory be known to all the people.' Aaron ain't say a word.
10.4: Then Moses called for Mishael and Elzaphan, Aaron's cousins (the sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle). He told them, 'Come get your kinfolk and take them outside the camp.'
10.5: So they came forward, picked up the bodies by their clothes, and carried them out the camp, just like Moses told them.

If you do, you'll die, and God's anger gonna hit the whole community. But the rest of the Israelites—your family—they can mourn for Nadab and Abihu and how the Lord struck them down.'
10.7: 'But y'all can't leave the entrance of the Tabernacle or you'll die, cause you been anointed with the Lord's oil.' So they did what Moses said.

10.9: 'You and your descendants must never drink wine or alcohol before coming into the Tabernacle. If y'all do, you'll die. This rule is permanent and applies to every generation.'
10.10: 'You gotta be able to tell the difference between what's holy and what's regular, between what's clean and what's unclean.'
10.11: 'And you gotta teach the Israelites all the Lord's commands that He gave through Moses.'
10.12: Then Moses told Aaron and his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, 'Take what's left of the grain offering, after the portion given to the Lord, and eat it beside the altar. It can't have yeast, cause it's most holy.'
10.13: 'You gotta eat it in a sacred place, cause it's y'all's share of the special gifts given to the Lord. That's what God commanded.'
10.14: 'But the breast and thigh that were lifted as a special offering? Y'all can eat them anywhere that's ceremonially clean. These parts are for y'all and y'all descendants as part of the peace offerings given by Israel.'
10.15: 'You gotta lift up the thigh and breast as a special offering to the Lord, along with the fat. These parts belong to y'all forever, just like the Lord commanded.'
10.16: Then Moses started looking for the goat that was offered as a sin offering. When he realized they burned it up, he got mad at Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons.
10.17: 'Why ain't y'all eat the sin offering in the sacred area?' he demanded. 'That offering is holy! The Lord gave it to y'all to remove the people's guilt and purify them, making them right with Him.'
10.18: 'Since its blood wasn't brought inside the Holy Place, y'all should've eaten the meat in the sacred area, like I told y'all to!'

11.1: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,

11.16: 'Eagle owl, short-eared owl, seagull, hawks of all kinds,'

11.24: 'These creatures will make y'all ceremonially unclean. If you touch their dead bodies, you unclean until evening.'

11.28: 'If you pick up its carcass, you gotta wash your clothes and you unclean till evening. These animals are unclean for y'all.'
11.29: 'These small creatures that scurry around are unclean: mole rat, rat, and all lizards,'
11.30: 'Gecko, monitor lizard, common lizard, sand lizard, and chameleon.'
11.31: 'All these little animals are unclean. If you touch one of them dead, you unclean till evening.'
11.32: 'If one of them dies and falls on something, that thing is unclean—whether it's wood, cloth, leather, or burlap. You gotta dip it in water, and it stays unclean till evening. Then it's clean again.'

11.34: 'If the water from that pot spills on food, that food is unclean. If you drinking from that pot, the drink is unclean.'
11.35: 'If the dead body of one of these animals falls on something, it's unclean—whether it's an oven or a stove, it gotta be destroyed cause it's contaminated.'
11.36: 'But if it falls into a spring or well, the water is still clean. But if somebody touches the dead body, they unclean.'
11.37: 'If the dead body lands on dry seed grain, the grain is still clean.'
11.38: 'But if the seed is wet when the dead body lands on it, the seed is unclean.'
11.39: 'If an animal y'all can eat dies and you touch its dead body, you unclean till evening.'
11.40: 'If you eat the meat or carry its carcass, you gotta wash your clothes and stay unclean till evening.'
11.41: 'All small animals that scurry on the ground nasty to y'all. Don't eat them.'
11.42: 'That includes animals that crawl on their bellies, walk on four legs, or got too many legs to count—don't eat none of them.'
11.43: 'Don't make y'all selves unclean by touching them or eating them.'
11.44: 'Cause I am the Lord your God, and y'all gotta set yourselves apart and be holy, cause I am holy. So don't defile y'all selves with these creatures.'
11.45: 'I'm the one who brought y'all outta Egypt so I could be your God. That's why y'all gotta be holy—cause I'm holy.'

12.2: 'Tell the people of Israel: If a woman gets pregnant and has a son, she gonna be ceremonially unclean for seven days, just like when she on her period.'

13.1: The Lord pulled up on Moses and Aaron and said,
13.2: "If somebody got a bump, a scab, or a light spot on their skin that look like it could be something serious, they need to go see Aaron the priest or one of his sons.
13.3: The priest gotta check them out—if the hair in that spot turned white and it look deep, like it's sitting under the skin, that's leprosy. The priest gotta call it like it is—unclean.
13.4: But if the spot ain't deep and the hair ain't turned white, then the priest gotta put them in quarantine for seven days.
13.5: On the seventh day, the priest gotta check again. If the spot ain't changed or spread, then he gotta isolate them for another seven days.
13.6: After another seven days, if the spot faded and ain't spread, the priest can clear them—it's just a scab. They gotta wash their clothes and they good.
13.7: But if that scab start spreading after the priest already checked them, they gotta go back.
13.8: If the priest sees it spreading for real, he gotta call it—unclean. That's leprosy.
13.9: If somebody got full-on leprosy, they gotta be brought to the priest.

13.11: If all that's there, that's an old case of leprosy. Ain't no need to quarantine, they just straight-up unclean.
13.12: But if the leprosy done spread everywhere, from head to toe,

13.15: If the priest sees that raw flesh, they gotta call it unclean, 'cause that means it's active.
13.16: If the raw flesh goes away and turns white, they gotta go back to the priest.
13.17: The priest gotta check them again—if it's all white now, they clean.
13.18: If somebody had a boil that healed up,
13.19: But then a white or reddish-white bump pops up where the boil was, they gotta see the priest.
13.20: If the priest sees white hair in it and it looks deep, he gotta call it unclean—it's a leprous sore from that boil.
13.21: But if the hair ain't white and it don't look deep, just a little faded, the priest gotta quarantine them for seven days.
13.23: But if it stays put, it's just a scar—they clean.
13.24: If somebody got burned and a reddish-white or white sore shows up in the burn,
13.25: The priest gotta check it out. If the hair in it turned white and it looks deep, that's leprosy from the burn. They unclean.
13.26: But if the hair ain't white and it ain't deep, just faded, they gotta be quarantined for seven days.
13.28: But if it stays put and don't spread, it's just a burn scar—they clean.
13.29: If somebody got a sore on their head or beard,
13.30: The priest gotta check if it's deep and got thin yellow hair in it. If so, that's a serious scalp disease—they unclean.
13.31: If it ain't deep and no yellow hair, quarantine them for seven days.
13.32: After seven days, if it ain't spread and no yellow hair grew,
13.33: They gotta shave everything but the sore, then stay quarantined another seven days.
13.34: If after that it still ain't spread and don't look deep, they clean—just gotta wash their clothes.
13.35: But if it spreads after they been cleared,
13.36: They unclean, no need to check for yellow hair.
13.37: If the sore stops spreading and black hair grows back, then they good.
13.38: If somebody got white spots on their skin,
13.39: The priest gotta check. If they just dull white patches, that's just a harmless skin condition—they clean.
13.40: If a man loses his hair and goes bald, he still clean.
13.41: If he just losing hair from the front, he still clean.
13.42: But if a reddish-white sore shows up on his bald head,
13.43: The priest gotta check—if it looks like leprosy,
13.44: Then that man got leprosy and he unclean. The priest gotta say it straight.
13.45: Anybody who got leprosy gotta wear torn clothes, let their hair stay wild, cover their mouth, and yell "Unclean! Unclean!"
13.46: As long as they got it, they unclean. They gotta live outside the camp, away from everybody else.
13.47: If a piece of clothing—whether wool, linen,
13.49: Starts getting weird greenish or reddish spots,
13.50: The priest gotta check it and quarantine it for seven days.
13.51: If the spots spread after seven days, it's unclean—active disease in the fabric.
13.53: But if the spots ain't spread,
13.54: The priest gotta tell them to wash it, then isolate it another seven days.
13.55: If the stain don't fade after washing, it's still unclean—it gotta be burned.
13.56: But if it fades, they can cut the stained part out.

13.58: If after another wash, the stain don't return, it's clean.

14.2: 'These are the rules for somebody trying to get ceremonially clean after a skin disease. Once they healed, they gotta go to the priest.'

14.33: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,

16.1: The Lord spoke to Moses after Aaron's two sons died for offering the wrong kind of fire before Him.
16.2: The Lord told Moses, 'Warn Aaron not to enter the Most Holy Place whenever he wants. If he does, he'll die. That's where the Ark's cover—the place of atonement—is, and I Myself am there in the cloud above it.'
16.3: 'When Aaron enters the sanctuary, he must bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.'
16.4: 'He gotta put on his linen tunic, linen undergarments, linen sash, and linen turban—these are sacred garments. But before he puts them on, he must bathe in water.'
16.5: 'Aaron must take from Israel's community two male goats for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.'
16.6: 'Aaron must sacrifice his own bull to make atonement for himself and his family.'
16.7: 'Then, he must take the two male goats and present them before the Lord at the Tabernacle entrance.'
16.8: 'He must cast lots to decide which goat is for the Lord and which will be sent into the wilderness of Azazel.'
16.9: 'The goat chosen for the Lord will be offered as a sin offering.'
16.10: 'The scapegoat will be kept alive, then sent into the wilderness to carry away the people's sins.'
16.11: 'Aaron must offer his own bull as a sin offering for himself and his family.'
16.12: 'Then, he will take a censer filled with burning coals from the altar and two handfuls of fragrant incense and bring them behind the inner curtain.'
16.13: 'He must put the incense on the burning coals so the cloud of incense covers the Ark's atonement cover—otherwise, he will die.'
16.14: 'Then, he must take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it seven times on the Ark's atonement cover.'
16.15: 'Next, Aaron must kill the first goat as a sin offering for the people and bring its blood behind the inner curtain.'
16.16: 'By doing this, he will purify the Most Holy Place and the whole Tabernacle from the sins of Israel.'
16.17: 'Nobody else is allowed inside the Tabernacle while Aaron does this purification. He must atone for himself, his family, and all the Israelites.'
16.18: 'Then Aaron must go to the altar and purify it with the blood of the bull and the goat.'
16.19: 'He must sprinkle the blood on the altar seven times to cleanse it from Israel's sins.'
16.20: 'When Aaron is done purifying the Most Holy Place, the Tabernacle, and the altar, he must bring forward the live goat.'
16.21: 'He will lay both hands on the goat's head and confess all of Israel's sins, wickedness, and rebellion over it—transferring their sins onto the goat.'
16.22: 'Then, a chosen man will lead the goat into the wilderness. As it goes, it will carry all of Israel's sins into a desolate land.'
16.23: 'After that, Aaron must go back into the Tabernacle, take off his linen garments, and leave them there.'
16.24: 'Then he must bathe in a sacred place, put on his regular clothes, and go out to sacrifice the burnt offering for himself and the people.'
16.25: 'He must burn all the fat of the sin offering on the altar.'
16.26: 'The man who led the scapegoat into the wilderness must wash his clothes, bathe, and then he can return to camp.'
16.27: 'The bull and the goat that were used for the sin offering must be taken outside the camp and burned completely—including their hides, organs, and dung.'
16.28: 'The person who burns them must wash their clothes, bathe, and then return to camp.'
16.29: 'On the tenth day of the seventh month, everyone must deny themselves (fast) and do no work—this applies to Israelites and foreigners alike. This is a permanent law.'
16.30: 'On this day, the priest will perform the atonement ceremony to purify y'all before the Lord and cleanse y'all from all your sins.'
16.31: 'It will be a Sabbath day of complete rest, and y'all must humble yourselves. This is a permanent law.'
16.32: 'Every year, the priest who is anointed and ordained to replace Aaron must carry out this atonement ritual. He must wear the holy linen garments.'
16.33: 'He must purify the Most Holy Place, the Tabernacle, the altar, the priests, and all the people of Israel.'
16.34: 'This must be done once every year to purify Israel from their sins and make them right with the Lord.'
16.35: Moses did everything exactly as the Lord commanded.

17.2: 'Tell Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel what I'm commanding.'
17.3: 'If any Israelite sacrifices a bull, lamb, or goat anywhere inside or outside the camp,'
17.4: 'Instead of bringing it to the Tabernacle entrance to offer it to the Lord, that person is as guilty as a murderer. They have shed blood and will be cut off from the community.'
17.5: 'This law is to stop folks from sacrificing animals out in the open fields and to make sure they bring them to the priest at the Tabernacle.'
17.6: 'Then the priest will splatter the blood against the altar at the Tabernacle entrance and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.'
17.7: 'The people must stop sacrificing to goat idols—that's unfaithful to the Lord. This rule stays forever, for every generation.'
