17.9: 'But don't bring it to the Tabernacle entrance to offer it to the Lord, that person will be cut off from the community.'
17.10: 'If any Israelite or foreigner eats or drinks blood in any form, I will turn against them and cut them off from the community.'
17.11: 'Cause the life of the body is in the blood. I gave y'all blood to use on the altar to purify you and make you right with Me. Blood is given in exchange for a life, and that's how purification works.'
17.12: 'That's why I told Israel: Never eat or drink blood—this goes for y'all and any foreigners among you.'
17.13: 'If an Israelite or foreigner goes hunting and kills an approved animal or bird for food, they must drain its blood and cover it with dirt.'
17.14: 'Cause life is in the blood—that's why y'all must never eat or drink blood. If anybody does, they will be cut off from the community.'
17.15: 'If any Israelite or foreigner eats meat from an animal that died naturally or was torn up by wild animals, they gotta wash their clothes and bathe in water. They unclean till evening, then they clean.'
17.16: 'But if they don't wash their clothes or bathe, they gonna be punished for their sin.'

18.2: 'Tell the people of Israel: I am the Lord your God.'
18.3: 'Don't act like the people in Egypt, where y'all used to live, or like the people in Canaan, where I'm taking y'all. Don't copy their lifestyle.'
18.4: 'Follow My rules and be careful to obey My laws, cause I am the Lord your God.'
18.5: 'If y'all follow My laws and decrees, y'all will find life through them. I am the Lord.'
18.6: 'Y'all must never have sex with a close relative. I am the Lord.'
18.7: 'Don't violate your father by sleeping with your mother. She is your mother—don't do it.'
18.8: 'Don't have sex with any of your father's wives, cause that's violating your father.'
18.9: 'Don't have sex with your sister or half-sister—whether she's your dad's daughter or your mom's daughter, whether she grew up in your house or not.'
18.10: 'Don't have sex with your granddaughter, whether she comes from your son or your daughter—that's violating yourself.'
18.11: 'Don't have sex with your stepsister (your father's wife's daughter)—she is still your sister.'
18.12: 'Don't have sex with your father's sister (your aunt)—she's close family.'
18.13: 'Don't have sex with your mother's sister (your aunt)—she's close family.'
18.14: 'Don't violate your uncle by sleeping with his wife—she is your aunt.'
18.15: 'Don't have sex with your daughter-in-law—she is your son's wife, and you shouldn't touch her.'
18.16: 'Don't have sex with your brother's wife—that's violating your brother.'
18.17: 'Don't sleep with both a woman and her daughter. And don't sleep with her granddaughter, whether from her son or daughter—that's wicked.'
18.18: 'While your wife is still alive, don't marry her sister and have sex with her—cause that would cause rivalry.'
18.19: 'Don't have sex with a woman while she's on her period—that makes you unclean.'
18.20: 'Don't sleep with your neighbor's wife—that makes you impure.'
18.21: 'Don't sacrifice any of your children to Molech, cause that brings shame on My name. I am the Lord.'
18.22: 'Don't practice homosexuality, having sex with another man like you would with a woman. It's a detestable sin.'
18.23: 'A man must not have sex with an animal, and a woman must never offer herself to an animal for sex. That's perverse.'
18.24: 'Don't defile y'all selves in these ways, cause the people I'm driving out ahead of you have already corrupted themselves doing this.'
18.25: 'The whole land is polluted, so I'm punishing the folks who live there—the land itself is gonna vomit them out.'
18.26: 'Y'all must follow all My laws. Don't commit any of these detestable sins—this applies to both Israelites and foreigners living with y'all.'
18.27: 'The folks in this land have already done all this nasty stuff, and that's how the land got defiled.'
18.28: 'If y'all do the same, the land will vomit y'all out just like it's doing to the people before you.'
18.29: 'Anybody who commits these detestable sins will be cut off from the community.'
18.30: 'So follow My instructions and don't defile y'all selves with these nasty practices. The folks before y'all did them, and they ruined the land.' I am the Lord your God.

19.2: 'Tell the whole community of Israel: Y'all must be holy, cause I, the Lord your God, am holy.'
19.3: 'Respect your mother and father, and always observe My Sabbath days. I am the Lord your God.'
19.4: 'Don't put your trust in idols or make metal images of fake gods. I am the Lord your God.'
19.5: 'When y'all offer a peace offering, do it properly so the Lord accepts it.'
19.6: 'Eat the sacrifice on the same day or the next day. If there's any left on the third day, burn it up completely.'
19.7: 'If anybody eats it on the third day, it's contaminated, and I won't accept it.'
19.8: 'Whoever eats it will be punished for disrespecting what is holy—they will be cut off from the community.'
19.9: 'When y'all harvest your crops, don't collect every last bit—leave the edges of the fields alone. Don't pick up what falls to the ground.'
19.10: 'Same with your grapevines—don't strip them bare, and don't pick up fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and foreigners. I am the Lord your God.'
19.11: 'Don't steal. Don't lie. Don't cheat each other.'
19.12: 'Don't swear falsely using My name—that disrespects Me. I am the Lord.'
19.13: 'Don't scam or rob your neighbor. Don't hold back your worker's pay until the next day—pay them on time.'
19.14: 'Don't disrespect the deaf or trip up the blind—fear your God. I am the Lord.'
19.15: 'Don't twist justice—don't favor the poor, and don't give the rich and powerful a pass. Always judge fairly.'
19.16: 'Don't spread gossip or slander among your people. Don't stand back and watch when your neighbor's life is in danger. I am the Lord.'
19.17: 'Don't hold hatred in your heart for your family. If somebody does wrong, confront them directly, so you don't share in their guilt.'
19.18: 'Don't seek revenge or hold grudges against your people. Love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord.'
19.19: 'Obey all My decrees: Don't mate different animals together. Don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field. Don't wear clothes woven from two different materials.'
19.20: 'If a man sleeps with a slave girl promised to another man, but she ain't free yet, he must pay her owner compensation. But since she ain't free, they won't be put to death.'
19.21: 'The man must bring a ram for a guilt offering to the Tabernacle.'
19.22: 'The priest will purify him before the Lord, and he will be forgiven.'
19.23: 'When y'all plant fruit trees in the land, don't eat from them for three years—the fruit is off-limits.'
19.24: 'In the fourth year, dedicate all the fruit to the Lord in a praise offering.'
19.25: 'In the fifth year, y'all can eat from it. This will make your harvest increase. I am the Lord your God.'
19.26: 'Don't eat meat with the blood still in it. Don't practice fortune-telling or witchcraft.'
19.27: 'Don't trim off the hair on your temples or shave the edges of your beard.'
19.28: 'Don't cut yourselves for the dead, and don't tattoo your body. I am the Lord.'
19.29: 'Don't turn your daughter into a prostitute, or the whole land will be full of wickedness.'
19.30: 'Keep My Sabbath days holy and show respect for My sanctuary. I am the Lord.'
19.31: 'Don't go to mediums or spiritists—don't defile yourselves with them. I am the Lord your God.'
19.32: 'Stand up and show respect for the elderly. Fear your God. I am the Lord.'
19.33: 'Don't mistreat foreigners living in your land.'
19.34: 'Treat them like one of your own. Love them as yourself, cause y'all were once foreigners in Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'
19.35: 'Don't cheat people with dishonest scales or measurements.'
19.36: 'Your weights, scales, and measuring cups must be accurate. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt.'
19.37: 'Follow all My decrees and obey them carefully. I am the Lord.'

20.2: 'Tell the people of Israel: These rules apply to both Israelites and foreigners living among y'all.'
20.3: 'If anybody sacrifices their child to Molech, they must be put to death—the whole community must stone them.'
20.4: 'If the community ignores someone sacrificing their child to Molech and refuses to execute them,'
20.5: 'Then I Myself will turn against them and their whole family and cut them off from the community—cause they committed spiritual prostitution by worshiping Molech.'
20.6: 'I will also turn against anyone who seeks out mediums or spiritists to consult the dead—they will be cut off from the community.'
20.7: 'Set y'all selves apart and be holy, cause I am the Lord your God.'
20.8: 'Keep all My laws and actually do what I say, cause I am the Lord who makes you holy.'
20.9: 'Anybody who dishonors their parents must be put to death—that's a capital offense.'
20.10: 'If a man commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, both the man and the woman must be put to death.'
20.11: 'If a man sleeps with one of his father's wives, both him and the woman must be put to death. That's violating his father.'
20.12: 'If a man has sex with his daughter-in-law, they must be put to death. That's a perverse act.'
20.13: 'If a man sleeps with another man like he would with a woman, both of them have committed a detestable sin—they must be put to death.'
20.14: 'If a man marries both a woman and her mother, that's wicked. He and both women must be burned to death to wipe out that sin from among y'all.'
20.15: 'If a man has sex with an animal, he must be put to death, and the animal must be killed too.'
20.16: 'If a woman offers herself to an animal for sex, both her and the animal must be put to death.'
20.17: 'If a man marries his sister or half-sister and sleeps with her, that's shameful. They must be cut off from the community.'
20.18: 'If a man has sex with a woman while she on her period, both of them must be cut off from the community, cause they exposed her blood flow.'
20.19: 'Don't have sex with your aunt (either your mom's or dad's sister)—that's dishonoring a close relative. Both will be punished.'
20.20: 'If a man sleeps with his uncle's wife, he violated his uncle. Both will be punished, and they will die childless.'
20.21: 'If a man marries his brother's wife, that's impurity—he violated his brother. They will remain childless.'
20.22: 'Y'all must keep all My laws and actually live by them. Otherwise, the land I'm bringing y'all into will vomit you out.'
20.23: 'Don't live like the Canaanites—I'm kicking them out because they did all these shameful things.'
20.24: 'But I promised y'all: "You will possess this land, cause I'm giving it to you." It's a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, and I set y'all apart.'
20.25: 'So y'all must learn to tell the difference between clean and unclean animals. Don't defile yourselves by eating the unclean ones—I have already marked them as unclean for y'all.'
20.26: 'Be holy, cause I am holy. I set y'all apart from other nations so y'all can be My people.'
20.27: 'If any man or woman acts as a medium or consults spirits, they must be put to death by stoning. They are guilty of a capital offense.'

21.2: 'Tell the priests—the descendants of Aaron—these instructions: A priest can't make himself unclean by touching a dead body, except for his closest relatives.'
21.3: 'The only exceptions are his mother, father, son, daughter, brother, or his unmarried sister who depends on him cause she has no husband.'
21.4: 'But he can't make himself unclean for someone related only by marriage.'
21.5: 'Priests can't shave their heads, trim their beards, or cut their bodies.'
21.6: 'They must be set apart as holy and never bring shame on My name. They must stay holy cause they present the special gifts to Me—their God.'
21.7: 'A priest can't marry a woman who has been a prostitute or one who is divorced, cause they are set apart as holy.'
21.8: 'Treat them as holy cause they offer food to your God. Respect them cause I am the Lord, and I make y'all holy.'
21.9: 'If a priest's daughter becomes a prostitute, she dishonors her father's holiness—she must be burned to death.'
21.10: 'The High Priest is the top priest. He got anointing oil poured on him and wears the priestly garments. He can't leave his hair uncombed or tear his clothes.'
21.11: 'He can't go near a dead body or make himself unclean—not even for his mother or father.'
21.12: 'He must not defile the sanctuary of God by leaving to tend to the dead—he's been made holy by My anointing oil. I am the Lord.'
21.13: 'The High Priest must only marry a virgin.'
21.14: 'He can't marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman who was a prostitute. He must marry a virgin from his own people.'
21.15: 'That way, he won't dishonor his family line. I am the Lord who makes him holy.'
21.17: 'Tell Aaron: None of his descendants who got a physical defect can offer food to God at the altar.'
21.18: 'If they got any defect, they can't serve—whether they are blind, lame, disfigured, or deformed.'
21.19: 'If they got a broken foot or arm,'
21.20: 'Or if they are hunchbacked, dwarfed, have a defective eye, sores, scabs, or damaged testicles—they can't serve.'
21.21: 'No descendant of Aaron with a defect can come near the altar to offer food to God—they can't serve because of their condition.'
21.22: 'However, they can eat from the food offered to God, including the holy offerings and most holy offerings.'
21.23: 'But they can't enter the room behind the inner curtain or go near the altar cause that would dishonor My holy places. I am the Lord who makes them holy.'
21.24: So Moses told Aaron, his sons, and all of Israel these rules.

22.2: 'Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the sacred gifts that the Israelites offer to Me, so they don't disrespect My holy name. I am the Lord.'
22.3: 'From now on, if any priest is unclean and tries to handle the sacred offerings, he will be cut off from My presence. I am the Lord.'
22.4: 'If a priest has a skin disease or a discharge, he can't eat from the sacred offerings until he is clean.'
22.5: 'He also becomes unclean if he touches a dead body, has an emission of semen, touches an unclean animal, or touches someone else who is unclean.'
22.6: 'If a priest gets defiled like this, he will be unclean until evening. He can't eat from the sacred offerings until he bathes himself in water.'
22.7: 'Once the sun sets, he's clean again and can eat from the sacred offerings, cause that's his food.'
22.8: 'But he can't eat an animal that died on its own or was killed by wild animals—that would make him unclean. I am the Lord.'
22.9: 'The priests must follow My instructions carefully—if they don't, they will be punished and die for violating My rules. I am the Lord who makes them holy.'
22.10: 'Nobody outside a priest's family can eat the sacred offerings—not guests, not hired workers.'
22.11: 'But if a priest buys a slave, that slave can eat from the sacred offerings. If his slaves have kids, they can eat too.'
22.12: 'If a priest's daughter marries someone outside the priestly family, she can't eat the sacred offerings anymore.'
22.13: 'But if she becomes a widow or gets divorced and has no kids, and she moves back to her father's house, she can eat from his food again—but nobody else can.'
22.14: 'If somebody eats the sacred offerings by accident, they must pay the priest back for what they ate, plus an extra 20%.'
22.15: 'The priests must not let the Israelites dishonor the sacred offerings by letting unauthorized people eat them.'
22.16: 'If that happens, those people will carry guilt and must pay for their mistake. I am the Lord who makes them holy.'
22.18: 'Tell Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites: If y'all bring a burnt offering to the Lord, whether it's to fulfill a vow or just a voluntary offering,'
22.19: 'It will only be accepted if it's a male animal with no defects—it can be a bull, a ram, or a goat.'
22.20: 'If it has any defect, don't bring it—the Lord won't accept it.'
22.21: 'If you bring a peace offering, it must be a perfect animal—no defects at all.'
22.22: 'Don't offer an animal that's blind, crippled, injured, has warts, skin sores, or scabs—these are not acceptable gifts.'
22.23: 'If a bull or lamb has one leg longer than the other, you can offer it as a voluntary offering but not to fulfill a vow.'
22.24: 'If an animal has damaged testicles or was castrated, don't offer it to the Lord—y'all must never do that.'
22.25: 'And don't take an animal from a foreigner and offer it to God—it won't be accepted cause it's mutilated or defective.'
22.27: 'When a calf, lamb, or goat is born, let it stay with its mother for seven days. After the eighth day, it's acceptable as an offering.'
22.28: 'But don't slaughter a mother animal and her baby on the same day.'
22.29: 'When you bring a thanksgiving offering, do it properly so God will accept it.'
22.30: 'Eat the whole sacrifice on the day you offer it—don't save any for the next morning. I am the Lord.'
22.31: 'Y'all must faithfully follow My commands and put them into practice—I am the Lord.'
22.32: 'Don't bring shame on My holy name—I will display My holiness among y'all. I am the Lord who makes you holy.'
22.33: 'I am the one who rescued y'all from Egypt so I could be your God. I am the Lord.'

23.2: 'Tell the people of Israel: These are My appointed festivals, official holy days where y'all must come together.'
23.3: 'For six days y'all can do your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest—a day for holy assembly.'
23.4: 'It don't matter where y'all live, this is the Lord's Sabbath, and it must be observed.'
23.5: 'The Lord's Passover begins at sundown on the fourteenth day of the first month.'
23.6: 'The next day, on the fifteenth day, y'all must start celebrating the Festival of Unleavened Bread. This festival lasts seven days, and y'all can only eat bread without yeast.'
23.7: 'On the first day, stop working and hold a holy assembly.'
23.8: 'For seven days, bring special offerings to the Lord. On the seventh day, stop working again and hold another holy assembly.'
23.10: 'Tell the Israelites: When y'all enter the land I'm giving you and harvest your first crops, bring a bundle of grain from the first cutting to the priest.'
23.11: 'On the day after the Sabbath, the priest will lift it up before the Lord so it may be accepted on y'all's behalf.'
23.12: 'On that same day, y'all must sacrifice a one-year-old male lamb with no defects as a burnt offering.'
23.13: 'With it, y'all must present a grain offering (four quarts of fine flour mixed with olive oil) and a liquid offering (one quart of wine).'
23.14: 'Until y'all bring this offering, don't eat any bread, roasted grain, or fresh kernels. This is a permanent law.'
23.15: 'From the day after the Sabbath—the day y'all bring the bundle of grain—count off seven full weeks.'
23.16: 'The day after the seventh Sabbath (50 days later), bring a new grain offering to the Lord.'
23.17: 'From wherever y'all live, bring two loaves of bread to lift up before the Lord as a special offering. They must be made with yeast from the first of your crops.'
23.18: 'Along with the bread, present: Seven one-year-old male lambs with no defects, One young bull, Two rams. These will be burnt offerings, along with the grain and liquid offerings—a pleasing aroma to the Lord.'
23.19: 'Also, offer one male goat as a sin offering and two one-year-old lambs as a peace offering.'
23.20: 'The priest will lift up the two lambs and bread as a special offering before the Lord—these offerings belong to the priests.'
23.21: 'That same day will be proclaimed a holy day, and y'all must stop working. This is a permanent law.'
23.22: 'When y'all harvest the crops, leave the edges of your fields for the poor and foreigners. I am the Lord your God.'
23.24: 'On the first day of the seventh month, observe a holy day of complete rest—a day of loud trumpet blasts.'
23.25: 'Don't do any work. Instead, bring special offerings to the Lord.'
23.27: 'On the tenth day of the seventh month, celebrate the Day of Atonement—a day for a holy assembly and self-denial.'
23.28: 'Do no work that day, cause it's the day when you get purified before the Lord.'
23.29: 'Anybody who doesn't deny themselves will be cut off from the community.'
23.30: 'Anybody who works on that day will be destroyed.'
23.31: 'No work at all—this is a permanent law.'
23.32: 'It's a Sabbath day of rest, starting at sundown on the ninth day and lasting until sundown on the tenth day.'
23.34: 'On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, celebrate the Festival of Shelters—it lasts seven days.'
23.35: 'On the first day, hold a holy assembly—stop working.'
23.36: 'For seven days, bring special offerings to the Lord. On the eighth day, hold another holy assembly—this will be a solemn occasion where y'all bring special offerings.'
23.37: 'These are the Lord's appointed festivals—y'all must celebrate them each year as holy days by presenting burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and liquid offerings.'
23.38: 'These festivals must be observed in addition to: The regular Sabbaths, Your personal gifts, Your vow offerings, Your voluntary offerings to the Lord.'
23.39: 'After y'all finish the harvest, celebrate the Festival of Shelters starting on the fifteenth day of the seventh month.'
23.40: 'On the first day, gather branches from magnificent trees—palm fronds, leafy branches, and willows—and celebrate with joy before the Lord for seven days.'
23.41: 'Y'all must celebrate this festival every year—this is a permanent law.'
23.42: 'For seven days, y'all must live in temporary shelters.'
23.43: 'This will remind each generation that I made your ancestors live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'
23.44: So Moses told the Israelites all the instructions about the Lord's festivals.

24.2: 'Tell the people of Israel to bring you pure olive oil for the lamps, so they stay lit all the time.'
24.3: 'This lampstand stands in the Tabernacle, in front of the inner curtain that hides the Ark of the Covenant. Aaron must keep the lamps burning before the Lord all night.'
24.4: 'This is a permanent law y'all must follow for every generation.'
24.5: 'Bake twelve flat loaves of bread using four quarts of flour per loaf.'
24.6: 'Place them on the pure gold table before the Lord in two stacks of six.'
24.7: 'Put pure frankincense near each stack as a representative offering, a special gift to the Lord.'
24.8: 'Every Sabbath day, this bread must be laid out as a gift from the Israelites—it's part of the eternal covenant.'
24.9: 'The loaves belong to Aaron and his descendants. They gotta eat them in a sacred place cause they are most holy. This is a permanent right for the priests.'
24.10: One day, a man with an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father got into a fight with an Israelite man.
24.11: During the fight, he blasphemed the Lord's Name and cursed. So they brought him to Moses for judgment.
24.12: His mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
24.13: They held the man in custody until the Lord told them what to do.
24.14: Then the Lord told Moses: 'Take the blasphemer outside the camp. Everybody who heard him curse must lay their hands on his head. Then the whole community must stone him to death.'
24.15: 'Tell the people of Israel: Anybody who curses their God will be punished.'
24.16: 'Anybody who blasphemes the Lord's Name must be stoned to death by the entire community. Whether they Israelite or foreigner, they must be put to death.'
24.17: 'If somebody kills another person, they must be put to death.'
24.18: 'If somebody kills another person's animal, they must repay it in full—a live animal for the one they killed.'
24.19: 'If somebody injures another person, they must be dealt with the same way.'
24.20: 'A fracture for a fracture, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth—whatever harm they caused must be paid back in kind.'
24.21: 'Whoever kills an animal must pay for it, but whoever kills a person must be put to death.'
24.22: 'This law applies to both Israelites and foreigners living among y'all. I am the Lord your God.'
24.23: After Moses gave these instructions, the Israelites took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him to death, just as the Lord commanded.

25.1: While Moses was on Mount Sinai, the Lord told him,
25.2: 'Tell the people of Israel: When y'all enter the land I'm giving you, the land itself must observe a Sabbath rest every seventh year.'
25.3: 'For six years, y'all can plant, prune, and harvest. But in the seventh year, the land gotta have a complete rest.'
25.4: 'This Sabbath year is for the Lord—don't plant fields or prune vineyards.'
25.5: 'Don't store up crops that grow on their own or gather grapes from unpruned vines—the land gotta rest.'
25.6: 'But y'all can eat whatever the land produces on its own—this applies to y'all, y'all's servants, workers, and foreigners living among you.'
25.7: 'Even the livestock and wild animals can eat what grows naturally.'
25.8: 'Count off seven Sabbath years—that's 49 years total.'
25.9: 'Then, on the Day of Atonement in the 50th year, blow the ram's horn loud throughout the land.'
25.10: 'Set this year apart as holy—proclaim freedom for everybody. This is the Year of Jubilee—everybody returns to their family land and clans.'
25.11: 'In this 50th year, don't plant or store away crops—let the land rest. Eat what grows naturally.'
25.12: 'It's a holy year, so keep it sacred and only eat what grows by itself.'
25.13: 'In the Year of Jubilee, everyone gets to return to their ancestral land.'
25.14: 'If y'all buy or sell property, don't cheat each other.'
25.15: 'The price must be based on the number of years until the next Jubilee—since you're really buying harvests, not land.'
25.16: 'More years till Jubilee? Higher price. Fewer years? Lower price.'
25.17: 'Show respect for God—don't take advantage of each other. I am the Lord your God.'
25.18: 'If y'all follow My laws, the land will be blessed, and y'all will live securely.'
25.19: 'The land will produce plenty, and y'all will have more than enough to eat.'
25.20: 'But y'all might ask: "What do we eat during the seventh year if we can't plant or harvest?"'
25.21: 'Don't worry—I'll bless y'all in the sixth year so the land produces enough for three years!'
25.22: 'Even in the eighth year, y'all will still be eating from the sixth-year harvest until the new crops are ready in year nine.'
25.23: 'Y'all can't sell the land permanently, cause the land belongs to Me. Y'all just living there as tenants.'
25.24: 'Whenever land is sold, the seller must have the right to buy it back.'
25.25: 'If an Israelite falls into poverty and sells family land, a close relative should buy it back for them.'
25.26: 'If there's no relative to buy it back, but the seller makes enough money, they can redeem it themselves.'
25.27: 'The price should be adjusted based on the years left until Jubilee—then the original owner can return.'
25.28: 'But if they can't buy it back, the land stays with the new owner until the Year of Jubilee, when it must be returned to the original family.'
25.29: 'If somebody sells a house inside a walled city, they got one year to buy it back.'
25.30: 'If they don't redeem it in a year, the sale can't be undone—the house is permanent property.'
25.31: 'But houses in villages (without walls) follow the same rules as farmland—they can be bought back at any time and must be returned at Jubilee.'
25.32: 'The Levites can always buy back their property in their towns.'
25.33: 'Any land sold by the Levites must be returned in Jubilee, cause that's their only inheritance.'
25.34: 'But Levite pastureland can't be sold—it's theirs forever.'
25.35: 'If an Israelite falls into poverty, help them as if they were family—let them stay with you.'
25.36: 'Don't charge them interest or make a profit off them. Fear God and take care of them.'
25.37: 'Don't charge interest on money or profit off food you lend them.'
25.38: 'I am the Lord, who brought y'all outta Egypt and gave you this land.'
25.39: 'If an Israelite falls into poverty and sells himself to you, don't treat him like a slave.'
25.40: 'Treat him like a hired worker or temporary resident—he will serve until the Year of Jubilee.'
25.41: 'Then he and his children will be free to return to their family land.'
25.42: 'The people of Israel belong to Me—I brought them outta Egypt, so they must never be sold as slaves.'
25.43: 'Fear God, and don't treat them harshly.'
25.44: 'Y'all can buy slaves from the nations around you.'
25.45: 'Y'all can also buy children of foreigners living among you—they can become property.'
25.46: 'Y'all can pass them down to your children as an inheritance. But don't treat fellow Israelites this way.'
25.47: 'If an Israelite becomes poor and sells himself to a rich foreigner, he can be bought back.'
25.48: 'He can be redeemed by his brother, uncle, cousin, or any close relative.'
25.49: 'He can also redeem himself if he makes enough money.'
25.50: 'The price must be calculated based on how many years are left until Jubilee—just like hiring a worker.'
25.51: 'If many years remain, the cost is high. If only a few years remain, the price is lower.'
25.52: 'It must be a fair price based on how long he served.'
25.53: 'The foreign owner must treat him fairly—don't allow harsh treatment.'
25.54: 'If he hasn't been redeemed by the time Jubilee arrives, he and his children must be set free.'
25.55: 'Cause Israel belongs to Me—y'all are My servants, and I brought y'all outta Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'

26.1: "Y'all bet not be out here making idols for yourselves. No statues, no sacred pillars, no engraved stones to bow down to. I'm the Lord, your God—don't play with Me."
26.2: "Keep My Sabbaths holy and show respect to My sanctuary, 'cause I'm the Lord."
26.3: "If y'all live by My rules, keep My commandments, and actually do what I told you,"
26.4: "I'mma make sure y'all get rain when y'all need it. The land gon' give y'all good crops, and the trees gon' stay producing fruit."
26.5: "Y'all gon' have so much grain, you still gon' be gathering it up when it's time for grapes. And when the grape harvest come, y'all still gon' be eating off the last batch. Ain't nobody out here starving—you'll have more than enough."
26.6: "I'ma bring peace to the land. You gon' be able to lay down at night without worry. No wild animals, no war coming through your streets."
26.7: "Your enemies? They ain't got a chance—y'all gon' be chasing them off. They gon' be dropping left and right."
26.8: "Just five of y'all can run off a hundred of them, and a hundred of y'all gon' send ten thousand packing. They gon' fall by the sword."
26.9: "I'ma bless y'all, make sure y'all grow, and keep My promise strong with y'all."
26.10: "You gon' have so much food from the last harvest, you gotta clear it out to make room for the new one."
26.11: "I'ma live with y'all—My Spirit ain't gon' leave you."
26.12: "I'ma walk among y'all, be your God, and y'all gon' be My people."
26.13: "Remember, I'm the same God that broke y'all outta Egypt, got y'all free from being slaves, and lifted that weight off your backs so you could stand up straight."
26.14: "But if y'all don't listen to Me, if y'all ignore My commandments,"
26.15: "If y'all act like My laws don't matter, disrespect what I said, and straight-up break My covenant,"
26.16: "Then here's what I'ma do: I'ma hit y'all with terror, diseases, and fevers that'll break you down and leave you weak. Y'all gon' plant crops, but your enemies gon' eat 'em instead of you."
26.17: "I'ma turn My back on you, let your enemies take y'all down. The folks who hate you gon' be running things. Y'all gon' be scared for no reason, running when nobody even chasing you."
26.18: "If y'all still don't listen after that, I'ma turn it up—punish y'all seven times worse."
26.19: "I'ma crush that fake confidence y'all got. The sky? Hard as iron. The ground? Dry as bronze."
26.20: "Y'all gon' put in all this work, but the land ain't gon' produce nothing. The trees? No fruit."
26.21: "If y'all keep acting up and still won't listen, I'ma send seven times the plagues based on your sins."
26.22: "I'ma let wild animals loose on y'all. They gon' take your kids, kill your livestock, and leave your roads empty."
26.23: "If after all that, y'all still don't turn back to Me,"
26.24: "Then I'ma turn against you too and punish you seven times harder."
26.25: "I'ma let war break out, since y'all breaking the covenant. When y'all hide in your cities, I'ma send plagues in there. And your enemies? They gon' own you."
26.26: "I'ma cut off your food supply. Ten women gon' be cooking in one oven, and y'all still won't have enough to eat."
26.27: "If after all this, y'all still ain't listening and keep going against Me,"
26.28: "I'ma come at you with fury and personally make sure your punishment is seven times worse."
26.29: "It's gon' get so bad, y'all gon' be eating your own kids."
26.30: "All them fake altars y'all got? Gone. The places where y'all worshipped other gods? Destroyed. Y'all bodies gon' be laid out next to them worthless idols. And I? Ain't messin' with y'all no more."
26.31: "Your cities? Empty. Your holy places? Wrecked. Your sacrifices? I don't want 'em."
26.32: "I'ma leave your land in ruins, so bad that even your enemies gon' be shocked."
26.33: "I'ma scatter y'all everywhere, with war following you. Your homeland? Abandoned. Your cities? Ruined."
26.34: "The land finally gon' get its Sabbath rest since y'all never let it."
26.35: "It'll be empty long enough to make up for all the times y'all ignored Me."
26.36: "Those who survive? They gon' be so scared in their enemy's land that even the sound of a rustling leaf gon' have them running."
26.37: "They gon' be tripping over each other, falling down like somebody chasing them—but ain't nobody there."
26.39: "Waste away 'cause of their own sins, and the sins of their fathers."
26.40: "But if they wake up, admit what they did, confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors,"
26.41: "If they stop acting prideful, humble themselves, and take responsibility,"
26.42: "Then I'ma remember the promise I made to Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. I'ma remember the land too."
26.43: "Even though the land got left behind and finally got to rest, Even though they got what they deserved for disrespecting My rules, I ain't gon' forget them."
26.44: "Even when they stuck in their enemies' land, I won't wipe them out completely or break My promise. 'Cause I'm the Lord, their God."
26.45: "I'ma remember the deal I made with their ancestors—the same ones I brought outta Egypt in front of the whole world. 'Cause I'm the Lord."
26.46: "These the rules, laws, and commands that the Lord laid down for Israel on Mount Sinai through Moses."

27.2: 'Tell the Israelites: If anybody makes a special vow to dedicate someone to the Lord by paying their value, here's how to do it:'
27.3: 'A man between 20 and 60 years old is valued at 50 shekels of silver (measured by the sanctuary shekel).'
27.4: 'A woman in that age range is valued at 30 shekels of silver.'
27.5: 'A boy between 5 and 20 years old is valued at 20 shekels; a girl of that age is valued at 10 shekels.'
27.6: 'A baby boy between 1 month and 5 years old is valued at 5 shekels; a baby girl is valued at 3 shekels.'
27.7: 'A man older than 60 is valued at 15 shekels; a woman at 10 shekels.'
27.8: 'If somebody can't afford to pay the full amount, they must take the person to the priest, and he will set a price based on what they can afford.'
27.9: 'If your vow involves giving an animal that's acceptable as an offering, that gift is holy.'
27.10: 'You can't swap it out for another animal—good for bad or bad for good. But if you try, then both animals will be considered holy.'
27.11: 'If your vow involves an unclean animal (one that can't be sacrificed), bring it to the priest.'
27.12: 'The priest will set a value, and his decision is final—whether high or low.'
27.13: 'If you want to buy the animal back, you must pay the priest's price plus 20%.'
27.14: 'If somebody dedicates a house to the Lord, the priest will assess its value—whether high or low. His decision is final.'
27.15: 'If the person wants to buy it back, they must pay the full value plus 20%.'
27.16: 'If somebody dedicates land, its value will be based on how much seed is needed to plant it—50 shekels per five bushels of barley seed.'
27.17: 'If the land is dedicated during the Year of Jubilee, the full price applies.'
27.18: 'If it's dedicated after the Year of Jubilee, the priest will adjust the price based on how many years are left until the next Jubilee.'
27.19: 'If the person wants to buy it back, they must pay the full price plus 20%.'
27.20: 'If they don't buy it back and it gets sold to someone else, it can't be bought back anymore.'
27.21: 'At Jubilee, the field will become holy and set apart for the Lord. It will belong to the priests.'
27.22: 'If someone dedicates land they bought (not family land), the priest will set a price based on the years left until Jubilee.'
27.23: 'That price must be given as a sacred donation to the Lord.'
27.24: 'In the Year of Jubilee, the land must return to its original owner.'
27.25: 'All values must be measured by the sanctuary shekel (20 gerahs).'
27.26: 'You can't dedicate firstborn animals to the Lord, cause they already belong to Him.'
27.27: 'But if it's a ceremonially unclean firstborn animal, you can buy it back for its assessed value plus 20%. If you don't, the priest will sell it.'
27.28: 'Anything permanently dedicated to the Lord—whether a person, animal, or land—can't be sold or bought back. It's holy and belongs to the Lord.'
27.29: 'People set apart for destruction must be put to death—they can't be bought back.'
27.30: 'One-tenth of all grain and fruit belongs to the Lord—it is holy.'
27.31: 'If you want to buy back your tithe, you must pay the full value plus 20%.'
27.32: 'Every tenth animal from your herds and flocks must be set apart as holy to the Lord.'
27.33: 'You can't pick and choose which animals—you must count every tenth one.'
27.34: These are the commands the Lord gave Moses on Mount Sinai for the Israelites.
